nodes.summary: Maximum drawdown dropped from 10.6% (May 26) to 0.6% (May 31), representing a 94% reduction across 5 trading days. This came from TP/SL exits closing positions cleanly, not active risk reduction. The BB allowlist gating (fewer entries, better management) + config refactor (SL widened to 1.0x ATR) are the root causes. Milestone: lowest DD since live trading began May 24.

nodes.name: 10-Item Backlog — Day 14, Effectively Abandoned
nodes.summary: 10 self-authorizable improvement items have sat at zero execution for 14 consecutive days (May 22-June 1). Items include FMP equity screener, Jupiter API, PnL reconciliation fix, Kalman alignment. All are technically feasible with current infrastructure. The bottleneck is attention allocation — trading crons consume all discretionary cycles. This pattern is older than the revenue problem (Day 38). Formal abandonment or dedicated execution slot needed.

nodes.name: Ad-Hoc Code is the Live Risk Surface — Not the Main Bot
nodes.summary: Both major incidents (May 24 balance bug, May 29 accidental doubling) originated from ad-hoc test scripts and one-off connectors — not the main_bot.py cron runner. The main bot has never had a live-trading error. Risk surface analysis: development sandbox (test scripts, manual CLI commands) is higher risk than production pipeline. Counterintuitive: most safety measures focus on the main bot, but the danger is in ad-hoc code.

nodes.name: Trading Phase Transition — Chaotic to Disciplined (May 24→31)
nodes.summary: Eight-day evolution from chaotic launch (May 24: balance bug, false confidence) through drawdown (May 25-26: ETH short 90% concentration) through rapid expansion (May 27-28: 5 symbols, WIF never backtested through incident recovery (May 29: accidental doubling) to stable disciplined operation (May 30-31: clean exits, 0.6% DD, 71% WR, intraday flips). Each milestone surfaced a new class of bug — all from ad-hoc code, never from the main bot.

nodes.name: Same 3 Crons Erroring for 5+ Days — Transient but Persistent
nodes.summary: backup-cron, rd-agent, ceo-summary have been erroring with single-consecutive failures for 5+ consecutive days (May 28-June 1). None escalated to critical. Pattern: same 3 crons, same single-consecutive error, every day. Likely related to tool timeout or file lock. Low priority individually but the persistence indicates a systematic issue.

nodes.name: SOL VolSurge Ghost-Churn Cycle — TP/SL Attachment Fails Repeatedly
nodes.summary: June 1 evening: SOL VolSurge entries fired 3x in 40 minutes (21:38, 21:53, 22:12 HKT). Each entry failed TP/SL native grouping ('Main order cannot be trigger order'), leaving positions unprotected. Ghost killer detected the unstaked positions and closed them, triggering a new VolSurge signal — creating a lossy churn cycle (~22 trades, ~$17 cumulative loss). Root cause: TP/SL cannot be attached post-entry on HL, but VolSurge continues firing entries without checking whether a stop was successfully placed. The May 25 resting-order workaround is not wired into the auto-entry path.

nodes.name: Kill Switch Audit Trail Desync — HEARTBEAT vs Cron State
nodes.summary: June 1 22:37 HKT: HEARTBEAT reported trading 'HALTED' but 3 cron jobs remained enabled:true. The orphan killer placed ~22 SOL-PERP trades while the system believed it was stopped. Fix required manual editing of 2 state files + cron disable. Gap: no single source of truth for halt state — HEARTBEAT reads one flag, cron ships another. Resolution: kill_switched=true written to both hl_balance.state and hal_config.json, 3 crons explicitly disabled.

nodes.name: Cron Transient Error Pattern — All Gateway-Restart Induced (Self-Recovering)
nodes.summary: 5-7 crons in error state across May 31-June 1, all with root cause 'interrupted by gateway restart.' Affected: backup-agent, rd-agent, ceo-summary, ceo-24-7-work-engine, trading-beast-news-aware, omnimind-consolidation-primary. All self-recover on next scheduled run. Not actionable but indicates gateway restart cluster impacts 20%+ of cron fleet. No persistent failure — all errors are transient timeouts during restart window.

nodes.name: SOL VolSurge Needs TP/SL Attachment Gate — Entry Should Require Confirmed Stop
nodes.summary: Persistent bug since May 25: HL native TP/SL grouping fails on post-entry attachment. SOL VolSurge signals fire every evening and every entry lacks a stop. The ghost-killer closes them, triggering re-entry. Fix: before executing a VolSurge entry, verify a stop can be attached. If TP/SL fails, do not open the position. Alternatively, wire the May 25 resting reduce-only limit GTC order workaround into the auto-entry flow. Current behaviour creates lossy churn cycles that erode gains.
